scope.flow: HypoVault performance-fee accounting via average cost basis and share transfers
scope.environment: HypoVault ERC20-style vault contract with userBasis accounting

statements.text: Alice holds a highly profitable position where market value exceeds her basis.
Bob holds a position at a loss with a high-cost basis.
Bob transfers his shares to Alice, triggering _transferBasis.
_transferBasis adds the incoming basis to the recipient's existing basis without distinguishing the recipient's pre-existing profitable position from the incoming position's financial history.
The merged basis produces an artificially inflated average cost basis in Alice's account that can be made equal to or greater than the current market value of the shares.
The calculated profit becomes zero or negative upon withdrawal, so the performance fee is completely eliminated.
Any two or more colluding users can systematically and completely evade performance fees, potentially reducing protocol fee income to near zero if widely adopted.
A secondary market for loss trading is created in which users with losing positions sell their high-cost basis to profitable users.
Performance fees should be charged on profitable withdrawals based on each user's own cost basis, and merging a transferred loss basis into a profitable position should not eliminate the fee.
Alice and Bob collude to transfer Bob's losing shares to Alice.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether transfers are permissionless or restricted; no unauthorized-caller condition is supported.
Report does not specify concrete numeric basis, market value, or fee amounts.
Fundamental unfairness (two-tiered system) and flawed economic model effects are claimed but omitted beyond the four-impact limit.
